label: copy-phase input token n (fed-back n, recall position >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input fed back at this step is the letter n (in_tok == n accounts for 100% of activation mass). It never fires on n in the original phase or at the delimiter, and is essentially silent when n is the first fed-back token (recall_idx 1, ~0% mass). The strongest activations come from an n near the start of the copy (recall positions 2-3, e.g. u t t n ... <DEL> u t t [n]). When n repeats, a second consecutive n fires more weakly (about 0.3-0.6 of the first). Some copy-phase n inputs do not fire at all (about 12% false positives), mostly late n steps. Rate of firing does not depend on L, first_tok or prev_tok.

issues: Core claims hold. All activation mass is in the copy phase (original and delimiter phases have 0 activations) and all of it is on in_tok == n. recall_idx 1 is nearly silent (126 of 500k steps). Test scores reproduce: P 0.879, R 0.998, F1 0.934.
Missed activations are negligible: 157 test steps holding 0.1% of mass, almost all tiny n:0.02-0.16 activations when n is the first fed-back token (recall_idx 1).

The explanation says the false positives are 'mostly late n steps'. The data do not support this. Precision is 0.82 at recall_idx==2 and 0.854 at recall_idx>=6, and it is also flat across to_go (0.84 at to_go 0, 0.88 at to_go >= 4).

The explanation says the feature does not depend on prev_tok. Firing frequency within the predicate does vary with context, though in a graded way. By prev_tok, precision ranges from 0.75 (prev '1') to 0.997 (prev 't'). By out_tok (the original token right after the n), it ranges from 0.62 to 0.998: o 0.68, t 0.65, z 0.69, 3 0.62, versus u 0.998, v 0.99, 1 0.99. So the ~12% false positives depend partly on neighbouring tokens. They are not scattered noise, but they don't form a clean class.

Excluding the low-precision next tokens (o, t, z, 3) raises test precision to 0.912 but drops recall to 0.897, for a test F1 of 0.905. That is worse than the original, so no better simple predicate was found.
The 'recall positions 2-3' peak is slightly off. By mass share, the peak is at recall_idx 3-4 (0.249 and 0.228), which is n at original index 2-3. Minor wording issue.
